summary: Ran full pytest suite (89 tests, 2 workers). Result: 88 passed, 1 FAILED. test_90_shared_guardian_across_siblings STILL FAILS with 409 duplicate_lead when creating a second sibling with the same parent_mobile. The claimed refinement in /app/backend/app/api/v1/crm_routes.py (contact AND student match) was NOT actually implemented — the code still uses OR logic where parent_mobile alone triggers a duplicate. Original Prompt-2 duplicate test (test_11 in test_crm_admissions.py) currently passes ONLY because of this bug: it uses a DIFFERENT student first_name ('Aria2' vs 'Aria') and NO student_dob, matching only on parent_mobile. If crm_routes is truly fixed to AND-logic, test_11's 409 assertion will break and must be relaxed to send identical student name+DOB.

critical.issue: Duplicate-detection rule was NOT refined as described. crm_routes.py:144-156 still uses $or across parent_mobile / parent_email / (name+DOB), so ANY contact overlap blocks — sibling case still returns 409. Must be changed to AND: duplicate only when (parent_mobile match OR parent_email match) AND (student_first_name+student_last_name+student_dob match, case-insensitive).

minor.issue: After the real fix lands, this test will fail. It posts student_first_name='Aria2' (different from lead1 'Aria') and omits student_dob, so under AND-logic it is NOT a duplicate. Update payload to use identical name+DOB (Aria/Kapoor/2018-04-11) with same parent_mobile to preserve semantic (same student re-submitted with same parent = duplicate).

action_items: Actually implement the described refinement in /app/backend/app/api/v1/crm_routes.py create_lead(): build contact_match ($or of parent_mobile/parent_email) and student_match (name+DOB triple, case-insensitive) as two separate query fragments and combine with $and; skip student_match when payload.student_dob is missing but then require BOTH contact AND some student signal to flag (or simply require both fragments — if no DOB provided, do not flag). Mirror same logic in check_duplicate for consistency.

Update test_crm_admissions.py::test_11 to submit identical student_first_name='Aria', student_last_name='Kapoor', student_dob='2018-04-11' along with same parent_mobile so it remains a true duplicate under the new AND rule.
Re-run full pytest suite to confirm 89/89 pass.
critical_code_review_comments: crm_routes.py:144-156 — Implementation does not match commit description. OR-of-three-clauses is materially different from AND-of-(contact, student).
check_duplicate (crm_routes.py:110-132) has the same OR bug; it will return false-positive duplicates for siblings sharing a parent phone. Should be kept in sync with create_lead logic.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Only 1 failing test: test_90_shared_guardian_across_siblings. Root cause is in crm_routes.py create_lead duplicate detection — OR logic instead of AND. Fixing that WILL likely break test_11 in test_crm_admissions.py unless payload is updated to send matching student name+DOB. After both changes, expect 89/89.
rca of the issue: In /app/backend/app/api/v1/crm_routes.py::create_lead (lines 144-156), the duplicate query is built as {'tenant_id': ..., '$or': [{'parent_mobile': ...}, {'parent_email': ...}, {student name+DOB triple}]}. Any single contact match therefore triggers 409. When test_90 admits Sibling2 with the same shared_mobile used by Sibling1, the first clause matches Sibling1's lead and returns 409 duplicate_lead. Fix: replace $or with $and of a contact-match subquery ($or of mobile/email) and a student-match subquery (regex name + exact DOB). Do the same in check_duplicate for consistency, and adjust test_11 payload to include identical student name+DOB so it still represents a true duplicate.
